title: A scribal exemplar strip with sliding windows and local alterations
method:
A paper strip carries a row of word cards. Draw cards independently from a bank of 24 consecutive public training folios with probability .80 or from all training folios otherwise, in each case weighted by paragraph-body word counts. After 35 lines replace the bank, and after seven lines start a fresh strip. Between consecutive lines move the window forward by three, four, or five cards uniformly and extend the strip as needed. The two streams for paragraph-opening and other lines independently draw line lengths from the corresponding public paragraph-line samples. An entry, exit, or singleton uses its own position register; the exit matches the preceding word's last stroke when that conditioning cell has at least 14 training observations. At each occupied body slot, write a local register word with probability .43, otherwise read the card. On .56 of card readings replace one internal stroke with another weighted by training counts for its two neighbors. Banks, line lengths, and registers are fitted to certain paragraph tokens on the public practice training pages only. No Currier, hand, section or ritual word meanings are provided. The standard manuscript four-word copy guard rejects colliding lines and demands a fresh copy. The independent copy control discards the strip each line; the literal copy control disables the stroke replacements.
Public practice protocol and limits: the primary specimen uses fixed seed 408 and contains 1,800 lines of each stream, 31,526 words and one line redrawn by the four-word guard. Seeds 409 and 410 serve as sensitivity checks. No parameters or seed were changed in response to the primary score. The exact-copy excess (F-017) on practice is 0.018843, and the one-edit excess (F-021) is 0.013376. The independent-strip control gives 0.006198 and 0.002606, respectively. The literal-copy control gives 0.055722 and 0.005869. In a paired order control, shuffle whole emitted paragraph lines only among slots of the same folio, same token count, and same opener status. Across 63 fixed shuffle seeds, the median one-edit excess is 0 and one shuffle meets or exceeds the primary value. The median control moves 312 of the 652 paragraph lines. The F-022 reference condition is met by seed 410, but the primary specimen is kept as planned. The cut places separate sampled folios consecutively and does not validate copying over physical page distances. Reuse of the training vocabulary is allowed; the control rejects four-word phrases from the full public transliteration solely as a copy guard.
